faq.q: What does the primary coil in a transformer do?
faq.a: The primary coil carries the incoming alternating current. Because that current keeps reversing, it makes a magnetic field that keeps growing, shrinking and flipping.
asks: What is the input coil of a transformer?

faq.q: Why does a transformer have an iron core?
faq.a: Iron carries magnetic fields far better than air. The core channels almost all of the primary coil's changing field through the secondary coil, so very little is wasted.
asks: What is the iron core for?

faq.q: How does the secondary coil get electricity without touching?
faq.a: The changing magnetic field passes through the secondary coil and induces a voltage in it. No wire joins the two coils; the energy crosses by magnetism.

faq.q: How does a transformer decide the output voltage?
faq.a: By the ratio of turns. If the secondary has half as many turns as the primary, the voltage halves; twice as many, and it doubles.

faq.q: Why don't transformers work with DC?
faq.a: A transformer needs a changing magnetic field. Steady direct current makes a steady field, which induces nothing in the secondary coil, so no voltage comes out.
asks: Can a transformer work on a battery?

facts: In a transformer the voltage ratio equals the turns ratio between the two coils.
Large power-grid transformers can be more than 99 percent efficient.

quiz.say: A transformer's secondary coil has half as many turns as its primary, and 240 volts goes in. What comes out?
quiz.show: A transformer's secondary coil has half as many turns as its primary, and 240 volts goes in. What comes out?
quiz.why: The voltage changes by the turns ratio: half the turns gives half the voltage, 120 volts.

wrong.1: Doubling needs more turns on the secondary, not fewer.
wrong.2: Different numbers of turns give a different voltage.
